label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Thanks for asking me, Deirdre, rather than just announcing it. I really appreciate having a chance to put this here before SMT.

I do understand the numbers, and I know Bronwyn needs the help with 24 little ones. I’m not going to fight the move, but I also don’t want to pretend it isn’t a big one for me. Noma has been with me in the Seahorses for three years, since my first year of teaching, and she basically trained me that year! She showed me everything from the sign-in sheets to managing the parent WhatsApp group without losing my mind. We’ve built such a lovely routine together, and I’m going to miss having her in the room.

My main concern is getting the new group settled while Charlene and I are also finding our feet together. Those first weeks of Grade R can be tough, with little ones crying at the gate, and it’s a lot of change at once. Luthando and Mia already know Noma from aftercare, and her isiXhosa songs at morning ring are such a special part of our day. The children ask for “Noma’s song” every day!

Could we please look at giving Charlene a day or two in the last week of term, 1–4 December, to meet Noma and see how the Seahorses routine works? I know Charlene’s official start date is only 11 January, so I’m not sure if that’s possible, but it would make such a difference.

And since Noma will be just across the courtyard, could she perhaps pop in for morning ring during the first week back from 14 January, even if it’s only for 15 minutes? It would give some of the children a familiar face while we settle in, and help Charlene learn the songs and routine too.

Thanks again for asking, Deirdre. I know there’s a lot to juggle, and I’d really appreciate it if you could take both handover requests to SMT.
